scope: Add a usable saved-search weighting for verified candidate experience. Score only recognized job skills supported by verified, user-approved, source-backed experience facts; persist and explain the selected-search result. Missing or unsupported experience remains UNKNOWN and neutral.

environment.frontend: local Vitest, TypeScript/Vite production build, connected Chromium
environment.delivery: local-only; no push or hosted automation

acceptance: The saved-search profile editor exposes a clearly described Verified experience dimension and persists weight edits through the existing profile API.
Experience scoring uses only facts marked verified and user-approved, with confidence at least 80 and a nonempty source; only normalized recognized skills shared with the job are scored.
Posting-provided experience signals cannot supply candidate experience. Missing or unmatched approved facts remain UNKNOWN, do not reduce the score, and do not enter its denominator.

Recalculation persists the weighted result and contribution explanation under the selected search. The connected browser readback verifies profile version, contribution value, provenance, and unchanged hard eligibility and other-search configuration.
No experience text, external request, AI request, or application submission is emitted by the connected workflow.

checks.evidence: 31 tests passed; 2 subtests passed. Connected Chromium workflow passed against an isolated SQLite fixture.
95 frontend test files and 540 tests passed.
TypeScript and Vite production build passed. Existing advisory: generated JavaScript is 750.46 kB, above the 500 kB warning threshold.

not_run: Full Python repository suite and PostgreSQL-specific persistence acceptance.
Hosted Actions and hosted review (disabled by local-only policy).
External job-source collection and real external application submission (OFF).
limitations: This closes the verified-experience weighting slice only. The broader MJ-REQ-117 configurable weighting requirement remains PARTIAL until all intended score dimensions and their user-facing scoring semantics are accepted together.
Skill recognition is bounded by the existing deterministic skill taxonomy; ambiguous, unrecognized, or missing facts remain UNKNOWN rather than inferred.
